Tesla’s rocket-shaped Robotaxi map in Houston is partly ‘fake’

EV
By Dr. Ethan Vance Chief EV & Battery Systems Fellow • via Electrek Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Electrek Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Tesla’s new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won’t actually pick you up, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and former Tesla employee.
  • McKanna rode the service after Monday’s expansion and called Houston “by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area” he has seen.
  • Official reporting verified via Electrek news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DR. ETHAN VANCE Chief EV & Battery Systems Fellow

The Electrification & Charging Infrastructure Horizon

Beyond the immediate headline, this development marks a critical inflection point in the broader EV transition. As automakers and charging networks race to lower consumer friction, the reporting from Electrek highlights that battery energy density, thermal management, and raw cost per kilowatt-hour remain the ultimate battlegrounds. For prospective EV buyers and fleet operators, tracking these operational metrics offers clear guidance on vehicle longevity and residual value.

Big Picture: Global battery production scale and grid upgrades will define whether mass-market adoption targets are met over the next 24 months.

Tesla’s new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won’t actually pick you up, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and former Tesla employee.

📌 The Core Development

McKanna rode the service after Monday’s expansion and called Houston “by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area” he has seen. One trip quote had him spending about 40 minutes in a Robotaxi to go two blocks.

On Monday, Tesla expanded its Houston Robotaxi geofence into the shape of a rocket . It took the small launch zone in northwest Harris County and stretched it into a long corridor down to downtown and Bellaire, announced with “Houston, we have liftoff.”

🔍 Background & Sector Context

McKanna runs Robotaxi Tracker, the crowdsourced site that tracks Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet and service areas, and he worked at Tesla this summer, so he knows the program better than most. He went to Houston to try it out. Here’s what he posted last night:

Another thing. Often AV service area maps advertised are kind of fake- they don’t actually go to everywhere in the polygon the provider publishes. Robotaxi Houston is probably by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area I’ve seen I get they were doing it so they could get… https://t.co/ILXIkmwGVp pic.twitter.com/yUfswZhQKF

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The video shows the Robotaxi app with a pickup pin dropped in downtown Houston, well inside the polygon Tesla published. The app refuses it: “Location not available. Move the map to select a different location.”

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

McKanna acknowledged that AV service area maps are often “kind of fake,” since operators don’t serve every street inside the polygon they advertise. But he singled out Houston as the worst case he’s seen and said he understands Tesla did it “so they could get the starship shape,” which doesn’t seem like a good reason to fake availability.
